subject: BENCHSARGENT
name: White Ships — connected cream and blue hulls, early structural shadows

styleSelection.reason: Pure watercolor. Broad transparent hull planes on warm cream paper; dry, controlled painted fittings. Pale foundation, dry, establish connected structural darks, dry, one middle-value wash. No ink or graphite.

families.referenceCue: Large curved blue-grey bow with cream oblique facets. Wash question: broad connected pale wash on dry paper, own wet overlap; dry, establish upper dark rim and lower shadow; dry, one connected middle wash. Small central fitting painted with a pointed round; soften only low-contrast turning edges.

Right hull is warm cream light, not brilliant white. Reserve irregular near-paper light planes; lightly tint adjacent planes. Blue diagonal and curved cast-shadow planes painted on dry paper; dark oval fittings use controlled round contacts. Keep internal light edges lost and structural edges firm.

Ochre and sienna rigging, golden anchor and slender cool supports. Pale foundation, dry, dark anchor junctions, dry, connected warm painted bodies. Wash question for each narrow body: round or rigger following fitted direction, with tapered ends and unpainted light side; no ink outlines.

Deep cool reflection joins the lower bow; green-turquoise water at right carries pale broken horizontal glints. Connected pale underwash, dry, two restrained structural glazes across bow and reflected wedge, dry, one middle water wash. No horizontal ground-deferral cutoff. Sparkle comes from reserved gaps and paper tooth, not added dots.

Rusty ochre rope crosses the pale right hull and green water diagonally. Dry-paper painted narrow warm shape, controlled medium load, continuous fitted body with target-supported interruptions. Dark junctions established before its final middle color; light flank preserved.
